overall: Revised determination: Committee violated the OML by inadequate executive session notice and by not convening in open session first on April 7; the notice violation was found intentional due to prior advice, with a hearing referral and recommended $500 penalty and orders.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 7 executive session notice was too vague because it did not name the nonunion personnel (the Superintendent) in the contract negotiation topic.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by providing insufficient detail in its April 7 meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to convene in open session before entering executive session on April 7, a required procedural step.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to first convene in open session prior to entering into executive session on April 7.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the notice and procedural violations were intentional; the AG found the notice violation intentional based on prior advice, not on any intent to deceive.
allegations.key_passage: We find this violation to be intentional based on the fact that the Committee had been previously advised that this conduct violated the law and not based on any finding that the Committee intended to deceive the public.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the AG noted it appeared the Committee did not take a roll call vote in open session on April 7 while members participated remotely. Reminder only.
allegations.key_passage: Even if a vote is unanimous, the law requires that the Committee conduct its votes by roll call when a member participates remotely and at all times during executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the AG noted the Committee approved the Superintendent's contract in executive session rather than returning to open session to vote. Reminder only.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law allows a public body to conduct contract negotiations with nonunion personnel in executive session, but does not authorize a public body to approve a contract in executive session.

remedy: Civil penalty of $500, recommended for the intentional notice violation and to be imposed after a hearing under 940 CMR 29.07(3)
Release of the April 7 executive session minutes to the public, with written notice to the AG of compliance within 30 days of receipt
Review by each Committee member of the AG's executive session training video (Video 4), with individual certification of compliance within 30 days
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We therefore find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law and order the Committee to release to the public the April 7 executive session meeting minutes.
